scope.behavior: After a completed baseline JPEG scan, the streaming decoder accepts bounded APP0-APP15 and COM segments before EOI, including repeated FF marker-fill bytes. It continues to reject unsupported markers, another SOS, malformed or truncated segments, and a truncated marker.
scope.fixture: synthetic 19x17 SOF0 4:2:0 grayscale-style JPEG with post-scan APP1 and COM payloads, embedded FF D9 bytes, repeated FF marker-fill bytes, and EOI; no clipboard, window, helper, package, or physical input
assertions: Direct streamed decoding accepts post-scan APP/COM segments and matches the corresponding fixture pixels and pinned jpeg-js 0.4.4 output.
The small production decoder route accepts the same fixture and matches pinned jpeg-js output; this low-memory fixture uses the jpeg-js fallback, not the production high-memory streaming branch.
The streaming decoder rejects an extra SOS, truncated APP segment, COM length below 2, stray byte, and trailing lone FF.
Production preflight accepts cumulative COM payload of exactly 1 MiB and exactly 4096 counted marker segments; it rejects 1 MiB+1 and 4097 segments with image_worker_capacity_exceeded.

preFixReproduction.failure: The new post-scan APP/COM fixture was rejected by EntropyReader.requireEndOfImage with image_source_invalid.

independentReview.reviewed: Boundary fixture counters and expected accept/reject values; post-scan marker and fill/truncation cases.
independentReview.scopeNote: The 19x17 production integration fixture uses the jpeg-js fallback because it is below the streaming threshold. Direct streaming parser behavior is covered, but production selection of the high-memory streaming branch with post-scan metadata is not verified.

limitations: Fixtures are synthetic and small; the suite does not cover a broad JPEG corpus, every legal marker sequence, or production high-memory streaming-branch integration for post-scan metadata.
No full T04 acceptance, product deadline, general hard memory bound, packaged behavior, or desktop workflow is established by this regression.
